profile.reading: AiNET's Beltsville, Maryland facility, identified by the short code WDC-1 on a dedicated Baxtel industry listing, sits at 11700 Montgomery Road, Beltsville, Maryland 20705, and serves as the company's home base. Founded in 1993 as a dial up internet service provider in Maryland, AiNET has grown into a regional data center, colocation, and fiber network operator serving the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor. The Baxtel listing describes this Beltsville building as a fully operational, single floor facility owned outright by AiNET, certified to SAS 70 Type II and TIA-942 standards, though the listing does not publicly disclose square footage or a specific power capacity figure for this building, restricting that detail behind a paid dataset request rather than publishing it openly. AiNET's own site describes the company's broader footprint as spanning the Washington DC and Baltimore corridor, including its larger CyberNAP facility in Glen Burnie, Maryland, a converted 300,000 square foot former department store roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade, already on file elsewhere in this registry. No square footage or MW figure could be confirmed for this specific Beltsville building this session despite a fresh attempt, an honest gap rather than a fabricated estimate.

profile.reading: AiNET's CyberNAP Glen Burnie facility occupies a converted three story former department store attached to a suburban mall at 7842 Ritchie Highway, Glen Burnie, Maryland 21061, roughly 10 miles north of Fort Meade. AiNET's own current CyberNAP page describes a 300,000 square foot facility on a 15 acre campus, with more than 80 megawatts of power capacity available from two separate electrical grids in a dual 2N redundant configuration, and power density exceeding 25 kilowatts per cabinet facility wide, positioning it as the largest standalone data center in the Maryland, Northern Virginia, and Washington DC region. A March 2012 Data Center Knowledge article on the building's conversion states each floor carries a 20 foot ceiling able to support heavy floor loads, capacity for up to 10,000 server cabinets, 1,500 parking spaces available for container deployment, and an opening planned for July 2012. The article identifies this as AiNET's third data center facility, and states the company, founded in 1993, targeted the site at enterprises and federal government agencies with a particular focus on Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility, or SCIF, requirements, given the proximity to Fort Meade's National Security Agency and Department of Defense operations. AiNET's own page describes three tiered security zones at the facility: a Commercial Security Zone with biometric access, an Advanced Security Zone exceeding NIST SP 800 requirements, and an Ultra Security Zone meeting NISPOM, DoD 8500, and ICD 705.2 and 705.3, or SCIF and DIACAP, standards. The facility functions as a carrier hotel with direct fiber interconnection to northeast corridor routes and access to AiNET's own DWDM fiber network. AiNET is headquartered at a separate Beltsville, Maryland facility already on file elsewhere in this registry.

reading:
AiNET, which trades online as ai.net, is a Maryland colocation and network operator founded in 1993 and based in Beltsville, inside the Washington and Baltimore corridor. It sits in this registry as a colocation provider, but a more accurate description is a regional carrier and data centre company built around federal and government customers rather than around cloud tenants. President Deepak Jain began his career as an information systems specialist at the National Security Agency, and Darrell Tanno serves as vice president of business development. The company sells colocation, fibre transport and cloud storage to enterprises, carriers and government agencies, and its marketing leans on proximity to federal buyers rather than on scale.

The site that defines AiNET is CyberNAP in Glen Burnie, Anne Arundel County. It is a converted department store attached to a suburban shopping mall, a three storey building of roughly 300,000 square feet with twenty foot ceilings and heavy floor loading, sitting on about fifteen acres. AiNET announced the conversion in March 2012 and opened it later that year as its third data centre, describing capacity for as many as 10,000 cabinets and around 1,500 parking spaces available for customer container deployments. The building's value to AiNET is location, a short drive from Fort Meade, home to the National Security Agency and to Defense Information Systems Agency operations. It is fitted out in three concentric security zones, and the company states that the middle zone exceeds NIST SP 800 requirements while the innermost zone is built to NISPOM, DoD 8500 and ICD 705 standards for sensitive compartmented information facilities. AiNET also describes CyberNAP as a carrier hotel with meet me rooms and its own dense wavelength fibre network, and lists further data centre space at Beltsville and Laurel.

On power, AiNET publishes that CyberNAP takes dual feeds carrying more than 80 megawatts from two separate independent substations. That number is utility service into the site, not critical IT load, and the company publishes no IT load figure for the building and no design density beyond a claim of more than 25 kilowatts per cabinet. The aggregate figures on the company home page, including more than 400 megawatts of electrical capacity and more than 2,200 on net data centres, describe the reach of AiNET's network and partner footprint rather than capacity AiNET owns or operates, and this registry does not treat them as site capacity. Anne Arundel County, Prince George's County and the City of Baltimore publish no project page, rezoning docket or capacity finding for any of these buildings, and no Maryland Public Service Commission siting case covers them, so the registry carries AiNET's Maryland sites, CyberNAP in Anne Arundel County, One Market Center in Baltimore and a Prince George's County building near the Beltsville headquarters, with no megawatt figure attached to any of them.
